name: Samsung A54 blob-free Linux stack replacement

mentions.name: Samsung A54 blob-free Linux stack replacement
mentions.description: A full-stack reverse engineering effort to properly own a Samsung A54 (Exynos 1380, Mali-G68): it boots a customized Linux 7.3 kernel without the Android layer (Wayland and WPE WebKit only), replaces the stock Wi-Fi/BT blob with a custom thin mac80211-based WLBT firmware, exploits USB control transfers for ACE in the PBL, reconstructs the LK-based S-Boot, uH and harx with byte-identical verification, patches mesa/panfrost, optimizes GPU kernels so STT/TTS run on GPU faster than CPU, enables NPU use via a custom-built toolchain, and targets pKVM with the original hypervisors removed — no binary blobs, with software and hardware changeable on the fly.
mentions.problem: The device is locked down with binary blobs and original hypervisors that prevent true ownership and on-the-fly control of its software and hardware.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’m reverse engineering and replacing the entire stack on Samsung A54 (Exynos 1380, Mali-G68), started with booting to a customized linux kernel (7.3) w/o Android layer at all (Wayland and WPE WebKit only), built a custom WLBT thin firmware to replace the original fat blob (using mac80211 as the foundation)
